requirement_title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement_text:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234
Type: bug

## Requirement

The analyzer does not work if `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

(The upstream issue contains no further text, repro or comments. Anything beyond this is derived.)

## Acceptance criteria

- With `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`, the MessagePack analyzer still reports its diagnostics (MsgPack0xx rules) for code that violates them. (derived)
- Behaviour with `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` matches version 3.1.0, where the analyzer worked. (derived)
- Behaviour with `SuppressSourceGeneration` unset or false does not change. (derived)
- Source generation itself stays suppressed when `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue.
verdict_reason: verified critical finding(s) backed by receipts: requirement-tests-1, logic-edge-1

checked.what: Existing SourceGenerator tests on head: 175/175 passed, 0 failed
Existing SourceGenerator tests on base: 167/167 passed, 0 failed
Receipts/SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (2/3), passes on head (3/3); refutes 1 lens claim(s): requirement-tests-2
Receipts/StringKeyedMembersStillGeneratedTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 1/2 failed
Receipts/StringKeyMemberLoopTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 1/1 failed
Mutation: 6 killed by the change's tests, 2 caught only by the existing suite, 4 survive the full suite, 0 compile errors, 0 timeouts (12 mutants on TypeCollector.cs)

findings.claim: Inverted condition in the second member loop. `if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey)) { stringMembers.Add(...) }` never adds a string-keyed member the first time it is seen. A duplicate would make `Add` throw. Every string-keyed member handled by this loop is therefore dropped from the object info. For normal (non-suppressed) types this breaks the requirement that behaviour with SuppressSourceGeneration unset does not change. The generated formatter silently omits those members, so their values are lost on serialize and deserialize.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.StringKeyedMembersStillGeneratedTests.StringKeyedFields_AppearInGeneratedFormatter and StringKeyedProperties_AppearInGeneratedFormatter. At least one should fail on head because the members are missing from the generated source. Confirm with a byte-diff: serialize a string-keyed [MessagePackObject] via base-built and head-built generated formatters and compare the map entries.

findings.claim: Inverted guard in the second member loop. The new code reads `if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey)) { stringMembers.Add(...) }`, while the three sibling hunks use `!ContainsKey`. For a first-seen string key the condition is false, so the member is never added. Every string-keyed member handled by this loop is silently dropped from the object info. The generated formatter then neither serializes nor deserializes it, which is silent data loss for normal map-mode types with no duplicate or mixed keys. Behaviour with SuppressSourceGeneration unset therefore changes, which violates the acceptance criteria.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.StringKeyMemberLoopTests.StringKeyedFieldAndPropertyAreBothInGeneratedFormatter. It defines a [MessagePackObject] with one [Key("...")] field and one [Key("...")] property, runs MessagePackGenerator through CSharpGeneratorDriver, and asserts that both member names appear in the generated sources. On head the member processed by the second loop is missing.

findings.claim: The string-key duplicate guard at the second site was written with an inverted condition (`if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(...)) Add`), so a string key is added only when it is already present. This is a source bug, and the tests that should expose it either do not reach this path or do not cover the unique-key case.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1179 negate-condition: if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey)) -> if (!stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey)); expected to survive because DuplicateStringKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure only has a Key("a") duplicate and checks the MsgPack005 diagnostic, and the string-key members collected on this path are never asserted on. Also run the existing generator snapshot tests with a field-based string-key type to see the formatter lose members.

findings.claim: The field loop (second site, lines ~1145-1182) has no test. All the added analyzer tests use properties, apart from the AllowPrivate test, which uses a private field with a single [Key(0)] and no duplicate or mixed-key case. The `continue` at 1148, the int duplicate guard at 1163 and the inverted string guard at 1179 therefore go unexercised by tests.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1163 remove-guard: if (!intMembers.ContainsKey(member.IntKey)) -> unconditional Add; expected to survive because no test declares duplicate [Key] on public fields.

findings.claim: no test in the suite detects remove-guard at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1179
no test in the suite detects delete-statement at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1181
the change's own tests do not catch mutants at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1163, 1165; the existing suite does

receipt_plan.detail: TypeCollector.cs:1163 negate-condition: if (!intMembers.ContainsKey(member.IntKey)) -> if (!(!intMembers.ContainsKey(member.IntKey))); TypeCollector.cs:1165 delete-statement: intMembers.Add(member.IntKey, (member, item.Type)); -> (statement deleted)

hunches.claim: In the same hunk, when a duplicate string key does occur, `ContainsKey` is true and `Dictionary.Add` is still called. It throws ArgumentException, so the generator (CS8785) and the analyzer (AD0001) still crash on a duplicate string key in this loop. This is the crash class the other hunks try to avoid.

receipt_plan.detail: Define a [MessagePackObject] type where two members reached by the second loop share [Key("x")]. Run VerifyCS.Test with SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck and observe AD0001 or CS8785 caused by ArgumentException 'An item with the same key has already been added'.

hunches.claim: The new `!intMembers.ContainsKey` / `!stringMembers.ContainsKey` guards silently discard a second member that reuses an existing key, and no diagnostic is reported. The generator now emits a formatter that loses that member's data, where before it failed loudly. The dynamic resolver rejects duplicate keys at runtime. So behaviour with SuppressSourceGeneration unset changes from a visible failure to silent omission of a member.

receipt_plan.detail: Define [MessagePackObject] public class C { [Key(0)] public int A { get; set; } [Key(0)] public int B { get; set; } }. Run the generator and assert that some diagnostic is reported or that B appears in the formatter. On head there is no diagnostic and B is absent from the generated formatter.

hunches.claim: In the second (constructor/record-style) member loop the string-key guard is inverted: `if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(...)) Add(...)` instead of `if (!ContainsKey)`. Distinct string keys are never added, so generated formatters and the analysis lose all string-keyed members. A duplicate key throws ArgumentException because Add is called on an existing key. This changes the output for existing users without opting in.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the generator snapshot tests for a [MessagePackObject] type with string keys, e.g. [Key("a")] properties set from a primary constructor or an init-only/record shape. The base build emits the members; the head build emits none. Add a duplicate [Key("a")] case to show the ArgumentException.

hunches.claim: The new `continue` after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys skips a member that was previously still added to the member maps. The generated formatter for types that mix key kinds therefore changes (member omitted, array length or key set differs), as does the set of diagnostics reported for them. Users with such types, which were previously reported and still generated, see different output.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a formatter for a type mixing [Key(0)] and [Key("a")] members with base and head and diff the output and the diagnostics (MsgPack005 and any follow-on). Run the existing analyzer and generator snapshot tests.

hunches.claim: The duplicate-key guards silently drop the second member with a duplicate key rather than throwing or reporting. Generated output for types with duplicate keys changes from a thrown exception to a formatter that omits the member. The hunks do not show a duplicate-key diagnostic being reported, so this might hide a user error.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyze a type with two members sharing [Key(0)] and assert that a diagnostic (MsgPack006) is reported with base and head; check that the generated output does not silently omit a member.

hunches.claim: Inverted guard in the second (constructor-parameter/record) path: `if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey))` calls Add only when the key already exists, so it throws ArgumentException on duplicate string keys, and it never adds new members. The sibling hunks use `!ContainsKey`. Generator/analyzer exceptions on attacker-irrelevant but user-controlled source can crash the analyzer. The string-key members are silently dropped, so generated formatters omit them. That silently weakens the generated serializer's coverage and leaves protections ineffective.

receipt_plan.detail: Run generator/analyzer tests with a [MessagePackObject] type with string keys (e.g. a record with [Key("a")] properties). Expect the member 'a' in the generated formatter. Under the head build it is absent, and duplicate string keys throw ArgumentException. Revert the condition to `!ContainsKey` and the test passes.

hunches.claim: In the string-key branch of the second member loop (field/property pass), the guard is inverted: `if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(...)) Add(...)` instead of `!ContainsKey`. Members are never added when the key is new, and a duplicate key triggers Add, which throws ArgumentException. This is the analyzer-crash path the change is meant to fix, and it also drops all string-keyed members from the collected type info.

receipt_plan.detail: Run a test with a [MessagePackObject] type that has two members with [Key("a")], covering this second loop (the field/property pass). Also check that a type with unique string keys gets all its members. The inverted condition throws on the duplicate and silently drops the unique members.

hunches.claim: The new tests only check the Foo type with duplicate keys and mixed keys, and the string-key duplicate test does not distinguish the inverted-guard bug. The test for the second loop (members without a constructor) is missing, so the mutation of the guard on that line is not killed.

receipt_plan.detail: Mutate the `stringMembers.ContainsKey` guard at TypeCollector.cs:1179 and run SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests. If the suite passes, the mutant survives.

hunches.claim: The `continue` added after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys at the first site (property loop) is not shown to be needed by any test. MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure uses properties, but its markup expects MsgPack005 on the mixed key and no MsgPack00x diagnostic from this path, so the diagnostic outcome is the same without the `continue`.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1008 delete-statement: continue; -> removed; expected to survive because the added tests do not assert that the mixed-key member is excluded from the collected members. Run SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure with the mutant.

hunches.claim: No test reproduces the reported bug that the analyzer produces nothing when SuppressSourceGeneration = true. The only change in the diff to the code path is the duplicate-key guards and `continue`, and the test hunks contain nothing on the analyzer entry point that skips suppressed types. SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed asserts that MsgPack011/016/017 stay silent, which cannot show a regression, and the other tests may already pass on base.

receipt_plan.detail: Run SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported and AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported against the base build. If they pass there, they do not reproduce the bug. The fix location for the suppress check is not among the hunks.

hunches.claim: The ExecutionTests tests (NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType, SuppressedTypeRoundTripsThroughDynamicResolver) do not exercise the analyzer or TypeCollector changes. They pass on base and head alike, so they provide no mutation coverage for the diff.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the ExecutionTests against the base build; expected to pass, showing they do not reproduce the bug.

hunches.claim: The README states the analyzer does not report MsgPack011, MsgPack016 or MsgPack017 for suppressed types, but the shown hunks contain no analyzer code that gates those diagnostics on SuppressSourceGeneration. The only tests are a negative test and the Execution tests. The documented behaviour is therefore unverified by the diff, and the real fix for the reported bug may live outside the shown scope.

receipt_plan.detail: Check where MsgPack011/016/017 are reported and whether they are gated on SuppressSourceGeneration. Then run SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed against the base and head builds.
